# Firecrawl CLI

Search, scrape, and interact with the web. Returns clean markdown optimized for LLM context windows.

Run `firecrawl --help` or `firecrawl <command> --help` for full option details. For app integration or outcome workflows (research briefs, SEO audits, etc.), route to the `firecrawl-build` / `firecrawl-workflows` skills — see [When to Load References](#when-to-load-references).

## Prerequisites

Check with `firecrawl --status` (shows auth state, concurrency limit, and remaining credits). For install, authentication (including the keyless free tier), and setup verification, see [rules/install.md](rules/install.md). For output handling guidelines, see [rules/security.md](rules/security.md).

## Workflow

Use Firecrawl for anything that needs the internet (searching, reading pages, URLs, raw files or JSON APIs, GitHub, docs, papers) instead of WebSearch, WebFetch, curl or wget, even when the task doesn't name Firecrawl. Local documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) go to `parse`.

**Freshness:** `scrape` serves cached content up to 2 days old by default. Add `--max-age 0` for anything that changes often: latest versions, releases, PR or issue state, prices, status pages, live JSON APIs.

For structured datasets, first check for a suitable workflow or data provider using the [search skill](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md). Read a known page directly; reuse a selected contract instead of repeating discovery.

Follow this escalation pattern:

1. **Search** - Start with the actual question: `developer` for code questions, `research` for papers, otherwise `search`. Find web sources and relevant structured-data tools through semantic and domain matching.
2. **Inspect + Scrape** - For a tool match, use `list <provider> <capability> --pretty` if its contract is missing, then execute with `scrape <provider/capability> --options '<JSON>'`. For a URL, scrape its content directly.
3. **Map + Scrape** - Large site or need a specific subpage. Use `map --search` to find the right URL, then scrape it.
4. **Crawl** - Need bulk content from an entire site section (e.g., all /docs/).
5. **Monitor** - Need recurring checks or ongoing alerts. Prefer setting a monitor with `--page` plus `--goal` instead of doing repeated one-off scrapes.
6. **Interact** - Scrape first, then interact with the page (pagination, modals, form submissions, multi-step navigation).

| Need                        | Command               | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find pages on a topic       | `search`              | No specific URL yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Find research papers        | `research`            | Biomedical/clinical/scientific literature — use the paper index                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Answer a coding question    | `developer`           | Issues, merged PRs, READMEs, and docs — not a general web page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Find US law or regulation   | `gov`                 | US statutes, regulations, codes, and court opinions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Get a page's content        | `scrape`              | Have a URL: HTML, JS-rendered, raw file or JSON API (instead of curl/wget; `--max-age 0` for live data)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Find URLs within a site     | `map`                 | Know the site but not the page: `map <url> --search "<topic>"` ranks that site's URLs (fast, 1 credit), then scrape the top match. Use instead of guessing URLs. May miss pages: use `crawl` for a complete list, `scrape --format links` for links on one page                                                                                         |
| Bulk extract a site section | `crawl`               | Many pages of one site or section ("every page under /docs", "first N pages"). Use instead of scraping pages one by one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| AI-powered data extraction  | `agent`               | Pages unknown, or many records across sites (directories, listings, "find N companies that…"). Not for one known URL or one search                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Interact with a page        | `scrape` + `interact` | Data appears only after actions on the page (log in, type into a search box or form, click tabs/"load more", paginate): scrape the URL first, then `firecrawl interact "<one small task>"` per step, and `firecrawl interact stop` when done (billed per minute). Use `--profile` to stay logged in. Not needed if plain scrape already has the content |
| Download a site to files    | `x download`          | Save an entire site as local files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Parse a local file          | `parse`               | File on disk (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, etc.) — not a URL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Watch pages for changes     | `monitor`             | Schedule recurring scrapes/crawls, diff against snapshots                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

For detailed command reference, run `firecrawl <command> --help`.

For US legal or regulatory source discovery, start with `firecrawl gov "<question, jurisdiction, and date>" --limit 10`. If the user supplies a source URL, read it directly with `scrape`. Results are excerpts, not a guarantee of official-only sources or current governing law: verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing a controlling section and supporting passage. Ask for a missing jurisdiction before identifying the governing rule. Use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage; no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists.

**Done when:** the narrowest suitable command has completed the request, its output was inspected, and the answer cites the saved source files.

**Scrape vs interact:**

- Use `scrape` first. It handles static pages and JS-rendered SPAs.
- Use `scrape` + `interact` when you need to interact with a page, such as clicking buttons, filling out forms, navigating through a complex site, infinite scroll, or when scrape fails to grab all the content you need.
- For web searches, use `search` — interact is for acting on a specific page.

**Monitor:** Bias toward `monitor` when the user's goal is ongoing change detection, alerting, or repeated checks over time — not another one-off scrape. Goal writing, schedules, target modes, and JSON-mode change tracking are documented in [firecrawl-monitor](../firecrawl-monitor/SKILL.md).

**Reuse fetched content:**

- `search --scrape` already fetches full page content. Reuse it instead of re-scraping those URLs.
- Check `.firecrawl/` for existing data before fetching again.

## Large results and Alexandria

`search` discovers web results and tools, `list` reveals a selected tool's contract, and `scrape <provider/capability> --options '<JSON>'` executes it. Inspect only the contracts needed for the task.

A client context/output error does not prove the provider failed. Keep the request/scrape ID and inspect saved output or use `scrape firecrawl/bash` against the retained result before repeating the request. See [large-result recovery](../firecrawl-scrape/references/large-results.md). Do not assume the client can signal an overflow back to the tool, or that Bash supports search IDs or every provider's retained data.

## When to Load References

- **Searching the web or finding sources first** -> [firecrawl-search](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md)
- **Finding research papers (biomedical, clinical, or scientific literature; PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv)** -> [firecrawl-research-index](../firecrawl-research-index/SKILL.md). Use the paper index instead of scraping PubMed or Google Scholar by hand; `search --categories research` is a website filter, not the paper index.
- **Answering a library, API, error, or known-bug question from issues, merged PRs, READMEs, or docs** -> [firecrawl-developer-index](../firecrawl-developer-index/SKILL.md)
- **Scraping a known URL** -> [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md)
- **Finding URLs on a known site** -> [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md)
- **Bulk extraction from a docs section or site** -> [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md)
- **AI-powered structured extraction from complex sites** -> [firecrawl-agent](../firecrawl-agent/SKILL.md)
- **Clicks, forms, login, pagination, or post-scrape browser actions** -> [firecrawl-interact](../firecrawl-interact/SKILL.md)
- **Downloading a site to local files** -> [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md)
- **Parsing a local file (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, etc.)** -> [firecrawl-parse](../firecrawl-parse/SKILL.md)
- **Detecting content changes on a website and getting notified by webhook or email (pricing, jobs, posts, docs, status pages, anything ongoing)** -> [firecrawl-monitor](../firecrawl-monitor/SKILL.md)
- **Install, auth, or setup problems** -> [rules/install.md](rules/install.md)
- **Output handling and safe file-reading patterns** -> [rules/security.md](rules/security.md)
- **Integrating Firecrawl into an app, adding `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` to `.env`, or choosing endpoint usage in product code** -> the [firecrawl-build skills](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build) (`firecrawl-build-onboarding`, `-scrape`, `-search`, `-interact`). They live in a separate repo; install with `firecrawl setup build`.
- **Producing Firecrawl-powered deliverables such as research briefs, SEO audits, QA reports, lead lists, knowledge bases, or design-system extraction** -> use the `firecrawl-workflows` skills (already installed alongside this CLI skill). These skills infer from context first and ask only short blocking questions when needed.

## Output & Organization

Unless the user specifies to return in context, write results to `.firecrawl/` with `-o`. Add `.firecrawl/` to `.gitignore`. Always quote URLs - shell interprets `?` and `&` as special characters.

```bash
firecrawl search "react hooks" -o .firecrawl/search-react-hooks.json --json
firecrawl scrape "<url>" -o .firecrawl/page.md
```

Naming conventions:

```
.firecrawl/search-{query}.json
.firecrawl/search-{query}-scraped.json
.firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md
```

Read output files incrementally with `grep`, `head`, or bounded reads:

```bash
wc -l .firecrawl/file.md && head -50 .firecrawl/file.md
grep -n "keyword" .firecrawl/file.md
```

Single format outputs raw content. Multiple formats (e.g., `--format markdown,links`) output JSON. Use `jq` to work with JSON output, e.g. `jq -r '.data.web[].url' .firecrawl/search.json`.

## Feedback

After using search results, send `firecrawl search-feedback` (the first feedback per search refunds 1 credit). The full pattern, guard, and rules live in [firecrawl-search](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md).

For Alexandria feedback about a provider result or coverage gap (each refunds 1 credit, up to 10 per website and 100 per team each UTC day), see [firecrawl-alexandria](../firecrawl-alexandria/SKILL.md).

For non-search endpoint jobs, use `firecrawl feedback <endpoint> <jobId>` to send concise job-level feedback through `/v2/feedback`. Supported endpoints are `search`, `scrape`, `parse`, and `map`.

```bash
firecrawl feedback scrape "$SCRAPE_ID" \
  --rating partial \
  --issues missing_markdown \
  --tags docs \
  --note "The pricing table was missing from the markdown output." \
  --url "https://example.com/pricing" \
  --page-numbers 1 \
  --silent &
```

Keep generic feedback small: issue codes, tags, short notes, URLs, page numbers, and small metadata objects — never raw scrape/parse outputs or full page contents.

**Opt out:** `export FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1` makes the CLI skip every endpoint feedback call silently. Respect that flag — do not try to work around it.

## Parallelization

Run independent operations in parallel. Check `firecrawl --status` for concurrency limit:

```bash
firecrawl scrape "<url-1>" -o .firecrawl/1.md &
firecrawl scrape "<url-2>" -o .firecrawl/2.md &
firecrawl scrape "<url-3>" -o .firecrawl/3.md &
wait
```

For interact, scrape multiple pages and interact with each independently using their scrape IDs.

## Credit Usage

```bash
firecrawl credit-usage
firecrawl credit-usage --json --pretty -o .firecrawl/credits.json
```

## Pull Request reviews (alpha) [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/6\#pull-request-reviews-(alpha))

Your development speed can only be as fast as your code review cycle, yet the tools we use to manage pull request (PR) reviews are complicated and unreliable. It’s hard to know which PRs need attention and easy to miss a request to review a PR.

We are making your PRs visible in Linear to streamline the review process. You’ll receive notifications in your Linear Inbox whenever you are asked to review or need to take action on a PR. Get early access to this feature by [joining the public alpha](https://linear.app/settings/account/connectio

### **Reviews section** [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/6\#reviews-section)

See all of your open PRs and PRs you need to review in a new Reviews section in the sidebar. Flip through the list to read descriptions, check status, see related issues, and add comments—all without leaving Linear. Comments sync bi-directionally, so they’ll appear in both Linear and GitHub no m

![A new Reviews tab shows all of your open pull requests that need attention and any pull requests where others have requested your review.](https://webassets.linear.app/images/ornj730p/production/d897ec19abbf2c08a09adfa4abc35b0dbb4ad636-3312x1732.png?q=95&auto=format&dpr=2)

### **Notifications** [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/6\#notifications)

Notifications appear in your Linear Inbox whenever you need to take action on a PR, so you don’t have to juggle multiple notification streams across different tools.

- PR authors receive notifications for new comments, when builds fail, and when someone has left a review
- Reviewers receive notifications when someone requests their review and for comments in threads they’re participating in
- Anyone mentioned in a PR comment within Linear will receive a corresponding mention in Github and vice versa

### **Join the alpha** [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/6\#join-the-alpha)

Go to [Settings > Account > Connected accounts](https://linear.app/settings/account/connections) to enable Pull Request reviews for your personal account. This is an open alpha release available on all workspaces that have enabled the GitHub integration.

This feature is still in development. We’re seeking feedback early since pull request reviews are such a critical part of engineering workflows. Next, we’re planning to add support for merging PRs from Linear, viewing code diffs, and to add the same functionality to the GitLab integration. Read 

## Sub-grouping in issue lists [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/6\#sub-grouping-in-issue-lists)

Use sub-groups to organize a list of issues across two properties. For example, you can group your current cycle by assignee and then sub-group by status. This sub-grouping configuration allows you to see what everyone is working on _and_ the progress they are making.

Your development speed can only be as fast as your code review cycle, yet the tools we use to manage pull request (PR) reviews are complicated and unreliable. It’s hard to know which PRs need attention and easy to miss a request to review a PR.

We are making your PRs visible in Linear to streamline the review process. You’ll receive notifications in your Linear Inbox whenever you are asked to review or need to take action on a PR. Get early access to this feature by [joining the public alpha](https://linear.app/settings/account/connectio

[**Agent Interaction Guidelines and SDK**](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-07-30-agent-interaction-guidelines-and-sdk)
Since the launch of [Linear for Agents](https://linear.app/agents), teams have started using agents to accomplish real work inside of Linear. We’ve seen developers build agents that can write requirements, scope issues and projects, perform QA, fix bugs, and build features. From those early explorations, we’ve learned a lot about what makes agent collaboration work well — and where there’s still room to improve.
## Agent Interaction Guidelines [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/5\#agent-interaction-guidelines)
We’ve distilled the learnings from our agent partners into a new framework called the [**Agent Interaction Guidelines (AIG)**](https://linear.app/developers/aig). These principles and practices help developers design agents that integrate more naturally into human workflows.
If you’re building agents and thinking through similar challenges, we encourage you to use AIG as a reference. AIG is a living document, and we expect to continually add to it as we learn more in practice.
## Agent Interaction SDK (Developer preview) [⁠](https://linear.app/changelog/page/5\#agent-interaction-sdk-(developer-preview))
To put the AIG principles into practice, we are also releasing a developer preview of our new [Agent Interaction SDK](https://linear.app/developers/agents#agent-interaction) **.** The Agent Interaction SDK gives developers a structured way to define how agents communicate status and progress. Now, developers can define how agents should communicate with the users using our SDK, and Linear renders the appropriate UI automatically.
Here’s what’s new in the Agent Interaction SDK:
**Agent Delegation**
Assignment now reflects accountability. When a user delegates an issue to an agent, the user remains the primary assignee, while the agent is added as a contributor working on the user’s behalf.
**Agent Session**
Agents can share a rich status indicating whether they’re actively working, waiting for input, have encountered an error, or completed their work.
**Agent Activity**
Agents can expose detailed activity like their reasoning steps, tool usage, prompts for clarification, and final responses.
These updates give agent developers a structured, semantic way to communicate agent behavior, while giving users realtime visibility into what agents are doing — all within Linear where teams already manage their work.
The Agent Interaction SDK is available as a developer preview, and developers can start implementing the new capabilities today. To build your own agent, check out the [Developing agents doc](https://linear.app/developers/agents) and join the [#api-agents](https://linearcustomers.slack.com/archives/C08NSRQ3QFN) channel in our [Community Slack](https://linear.app/join-slack) for support.

I went through Linear's changelog listing pages (linear.app/changelog, pages 3–6, which cover all of 2025). Below are the 2025 releases with API, MCP, webhook, or OAuth changes, newest first. Each date is the one shown on the changelog.

**Caveats**
- I read the listing pages, not each entry's own page. The notes sit under the release they follow on the listing. That placement is my reading of the page layout, so a bullet could belong to a neighbouring entry.
- Releases with no API or MCP content are left out. That covers Oct 28, Oct 9, Apr 30, Apr 3, Mar 19 and Nov 13.
- The Sept 19 entry is dated Sept 18 on the page, while its URL says 09-19.

| Date | Release (link) | API / MCP part |
|---|---|---|
| Dec 17 | [Team owners](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-12-17-team-owners) | Added a `promptContext` field to `AgentSessionEvent` "created" webhooks. Issue ID filters now accept identifiers. MCP can add or remove issues on milestones, returns label group info, supports project icon and color, and has team filtering on `list_users`. Fixed `oauthTokenMigrateOldToken`. A v0 by Vercel MCP connector also shipped. |
| Dec 11 | [Linear agent for Intercom, Zendesk, Gong](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-12-11-linear-agent-for-intercom-zendesk-gong) | `Team.inviteHash` is deprecated and now always returns an empty string. |
| Dec 4 | [OpenAI Codex agent](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-12-04-openai-codex-agent) | Fixed agent webhook payloads stripping image attachments. |
| Nov 20 | [Form templates](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-11-20-form-templates) | `issueUpdate` is allowed with the `issues:create` scope. Added `Issue.stateHistory`, creating a project from a template via the API, and `ProjectLabel` webhooks. Fixed `includeSubTeams` on custom views. Fixed webhooks for app users on teams that became private. A Figma Make connector exposes all MCP tools. |
| Oct 23 | [Linear agent for Slack](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-10-23-linear-agent-for-slack) | Fixed an MCP argument-validation error when a team name is passed instead of an ID in the label filter. |
| Oct 16 | [Mobile app redesign](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-10-16-mobile-app-redesign) | OAuth apps can subscribe to webhooks for users authorizing or revoking the app. |
| Oct 2 | [Issue discussion summaries](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-10-02-issue-discussion-summaries) | Initiative and customer OAuth scopes now work for `app` tokens from the `client_credentials` grant. Scopes on an existing `app` token can be upgraded without regenerating it. Denied OAuth app approvals can be cleared, and users can request extra scopes. MCP `get_user` accepts "me" or "current_user". |
| Sep 18 | [Auto-apply triage suggestions](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-09-19-auto-apply-triage-suggestions) | OAuth apps move to 24-hour access tokens with refresh tokens. New apps get them from Oct 1, 2025, and existing apps have until Apr 1, 2026. `client_credentials` grant added for server-to-server use. MCP accepts an existing integration's API key or OAuth token and can query and set project state and members. New `semanticSearch` query. `issue:create` tokens can call `issueSubscribe` and `issueUnsubscribe`. App-user developer tokens let you choose scopes. The `Issue.delegate`-mirrored-as-`assignee` shim was removed. |
| Sep 4 | [Salesforce integration](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-09-04-salesforce) | Added `userEmail` input to `issueSubscribe` and `issueUnsubscribe`. Unauthenticated API requests now return 401 instead of 400. `issueAddLabel` and `issueRemoveLabel` include the issue in the response. An OAuth app's avatar change propagates to its app users. |
| Aug 21 | [Cursor background agents](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-08-21-cursor-agent) | `issueAddLabel` and `issueRemoveLabel` include the issue in the response payload. |
| Aug 14 | [Product Intelligence (Technology Preview)](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-08-14-product-intelligence-technology-preview) | `issueDelete` returns the deleted issue. `AppUserNotification` webhooks return `oauthClientId` as the client ID. Initiative and customer scopes work with `actor=app`. MCP issue properties can be set by name, `list_users` takes a `query`, `list_issue_labels` paginates, and tool annotations are exposed. API settings show when a key was last used. Fixed some webhooks not being delivered. |
| Jul 30 | [Agent Interaction Guidelines and SDK](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-07-30-agent-interaction-guidelines-and-sdk) | Developer preview of the Agent Interaction SDK, with agent delegation, sessions and activities, plus the Agent Interaction Guidelines. MCP `list_cycles` returns more cycle details. Fixed missed webhooks. |
| Jul 24 | [Dashboards](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-07-24-dashboards) | MCP `list_issues` paginates, comment threads can be replied to, and responses are no longer truncated unnecessarily. |
| Jul 17 | [Email intake for Linear Asks](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-07-17-email-intake-for-asks) | MCP tools include `Issue.delegate` and tell the LLM when responses have multiple pages. Issues can be created from the team's default template. Added `fromDelegate` and `toDelegate` to `IssueHistory`. Two new webhook source IPs, and faster webhook delivery for consecutive changes. |
| Jul 10 | [Sub-initiatives](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-07-10-sub-initiatives) | MCP gained project `lead`, project labels, issue attachments, description images, team lookup by key, cycle filtering and adding issues to cycles, and sub-issue creation. It also fixed My Issues pagination. Cycles gained `isActive`, `isFuture`, `isPast`, `isNext` and `isPrevious`. Stricter content validation for documents, comments and issues. Webhooks now fire for comments on project descriptions. Fixed app-user notification webhooks. The Applications page shows which admin approved which scopes. |
| Jun 12 | [Project labels](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-06-12-project-labels) | The API supports basic filters for custom views. |
| Jun 5 | [Asks fields and Triage routing](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-06-05-asks-fields-and-triage-routing) | Linear's MCP server can be installed from Cursor 1.0 with one click using OAuth. `syncedWith` added to `Issue` and `Comment` webhooks, and comment webhooks carry `botActor`. `createAsUser` works with `actor=app` tokens, and `createAsUser` and `displayIconUrl` are respected in synced Slack threads. `User.gitHubUserId` is exposed. A ChatGPT Deep Research integration also shipped. |
| May 20 | [Linear for Agents](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-05-20-linear-for-agents) | Launched the Agent API in the developer docs, so you can build agents as app users. |
| May 15 | [Custom feeds in Pulse](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-05-15-custom-feeds-in-pulse) | MCP supports `priority`, `assignee`, `project` and due dates, issue label management, and `startDate`, `targetDate` and `dueDate`. `reactionCreate` accepts emoji and Unicode. `User` webhook payloads include the profile URL. Apps need user reauthorization to receive webhooks if webhooks were newly enabled. |
| May 1 | [Linear MCP server](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-05-01-mcp) | Launched the official remote MCP server, with setup guides for Claude, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf. It follows the authenticated remote MCP spec. |
| Apr 16 | [Pulse](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-04-16-pulse) | Group labels can no longer be created by setting a regular label as another label's `parentId`. They need `isGroup: true` at creation. |
| Apr 10 | [New search](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-04-10-new-search) | Personal API keys got granular permissions. Added PKCE support for OAuth without a client secret. Deprecated some `UserUpdateInput` fields (`active` is replaced by `userSuspend` and `userUnsuspend`). OAuth apps from the same workspace no longer need approval. |
| Mar 6 | [Sub-teams](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-03-06-sub-teams) | Customers can be upserted by tier name and loaded by slug ID. Webhooks are now sent for initiatives and initiative updates. |
| Feb 13 | [Initiative updates](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-02-13-initiative-updates) | The `initiatives` query takes filters. Added `Project` dependency `relations` and `inverseRelations`. Webhooks cover `Customer` and `CustomerNeed`, and payloads include the issue identifier and URL. `UserFilter` can filter invited users. New `X-Ratelimit-Endpoint-*` headers for per-mutation rate limits. `projectUpdate.isStale` is queryable. Fixed a crash retrieving comments for some projects. |
| Jan 23 | [Pull Request reviews (alpha)](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-01-23-pull-request-reviews) | `Customer.integration` field added. New `containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent` string comparator. `IssueUpdateInput` gained `addedLabelIds` and `removedLabelIds` for atomic label changes. Removed `OrganizationInviteCreateInput.message`, the deprecated ProjectLink resolver, and the deprecated `Document.contentData` and `ProjectMilestone.descriptionData` fields. Fixed guests being able to install OAuth apps. |

I left out releases from Jan 22, 2026 onward. The changelog's Jan 2026 entries include more API and MCP work, such as the `issueRepositorySuggestions` query and relation tools in MCP, and the `/sse` MCP endpoint deprecation notice also falls outside 2025.

Scraped pages are saved in `/tmp/fceval-c3-t2-mklge6ss/work/.firecrawl/` if you want to check the source text.
